full_judgment:
Khondker Musa Khaled J : Both the above mentioned cases having common question of law are heard together and taken up for disposal by this common judgment. 

 2. These two separate Rules, under section 561A of Code of Criminal Procedure, were issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the proceedings of Special Case No.14 of 2007 arising out of Tejgaon PS Case No.32 dated 21-1-2007, corresponding with ACCGR No.10 of 2007 under sections 201/409 /420 /447(Ka)/109 of the Penal Code read with section 5(2) of the Anti-Corruption Act, 1947, now pending before the Special Judge, Court No.5, Dhaka should not be quashed or any other order passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

 3. At the time of issuance of these Rules further proceedings were stayed and the accused-petitioner Tarikul Islam Khan was also enlarged on ad interim bail in connection with Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.15284 of 2008. 

 4. The relevant facts necessary for disposal of the Rules, in short, are that Mr Md Jahangir Alam, Assistant Director, Anti-Corruption Commission, Moulvibazar, lodged FIR with Tejgaon Police Station against these two accused-petitioners and many others under sections 409/420/109 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Anti-Corruption Act, 1947 alleging that the accused-petitioner Tarikul Islam Khan being Assistant Vice-President and Branch Manager of the Oriental Bank, Kawranbazar, in collusion with other FIR-named accused-petitioners, introduced fictitious persons in the matter of opening account in the bank and managed to obtain sanction of loan money and on depositing the money to their fake account numbers, misappropriated huge amount of money from the bank and that they have manufactured many vouchers for the purpose by resorting to forgery. During investigation materials were collected to proceed against and the Investigating Officer submitted charge sheet against six persons including the four FIR named accused-persons. The named Accused-petitioner Sultan Mahmud Hero of Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 5950 of 2008 was not named in the FIR but his complicity was revealed during the investigation. It is alleged that he identified fake account holders at the time of opening bank accounts, and accordingly, he has been made accused. 

 5. After submission of the investigation report, the case was transferred to the Special Judge, Court No. 5, Dhaka for holding trial. At this stage, on 29-11-2007, the prosecution side submitted an application for holding further investigation in his case in view of section 222(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure and the learned Special Judge on accepting the application, referred the case for further investigation by the Anti-Corruption Commission. 

 6. Being aggrieved, the accused-petitioner preferred these applications and obtained Rules mainly on the common ground that invoking Emergency Power Rules, 2007 in holding trial of the case was illegal and, as such, continuation of the proceeding under the Emergency Power Rules would be abuse of the process of the Court. It is also stated in the applications that no legal sanction was taken before submission of the charge sheet, which is also a clear violation of section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. It is also stated therein that sanction of the Government was necessary under Rule 19(Yeon) of the Emergency Power Rules and the said sanction not being taken, the prosecution has violated Emergency Power Rules rendering it liable to be quashed. It is further stated that the learned Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka illegally invoked Rule 19(Yeon) of the Emergency Power Rules, although he is not unauthorised person to give approval in the matter of holding trial under the Emergency Power Rules 2007. 

 7. None appears to represent the accused-petitioners in either of the Criminal Miscellaneous Cases when those are taken up for hearing. 

 8. We have heard the learned Advocates, Mr Khurshid Alam Khan and Mr Syed Mizanur Rahman, who have appeared before us in Criminal Miscellaneous Case Nos. 5950 of 2008 and 15284 of 2008 respectively on behalf of the opposite party No. 2. Anti-Corruption Commission. According to their submissions, the case being under sections 409/420/109 read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, are all schedule offences of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and, as such, the case automatically comes within jurisdiction of the Special Judge in view of Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules to hold trial under Emergency Power Rules, 2007. As such, separate sanction under Rule 19(Yeon) of the Emergency Power Rules is not at all necessary in this case. It is initiated by Anti-Corruption Commission and investigated by its authorised officer and sanction was obtained before submitting charge sheet. It is submitted that huge amount of money was misappropriated by the officers of the Bank in connivance with some persons outside. Accordingly, the case has been initiated and charge sheet submitted under the above mentioned schedule offences of the Anti-Corruption Commission on obtaining proper sanction as required under section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004. It is submitted that the sanction was accorded by the Commission on 2-10-2007, which is available in the police report itself. It is also submitted that due to some technical difficulties in bringing all the occurrences of misappropriation which took place during a long time, in one case, an application was submitted on behalf of the prosecution and order of further investigation was obtained to get it regularised. It is also pointed out that accused-petitioner Tarikul Islam Khan, being an employee of the Oriental Bank, is a public servant within the meaning of section 110 of the Bank Company Act, 1991 and there is no illegality in holding trial of outsiders along with public servants who committed the offences in collusion with each other. It is submitted that since there is no substantial ground in the applications under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashment of the proceedings, the Rules issued in the aforesaid two cases are liable to be discharged. 

 9. On perusal of the FIR and charge sheet, it appears that there are clear allegations against both the accused-petitioners and those allegations are not preposterous in nature, rather those attract the elements of the alleged offences, which obviously come within the schedule offences of Anti-Corruption Commission, Act, 2004. Accordingly, the case falls within the provision of Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules 2007. Therefore, the question raised as to the legality of inclusion of the case under the Emergency Power Rules does not bear any substance. 

 10. It further appears that the authorised officer of the Anti-Corruption Commission conducted investigation in this case and submitted report and there is also sanction of the Anti-Corruption Commission for submission of the charge sheet against the accused-persons. So, it is clear that after due compliance of the section 32 of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004, cognizance was taken by the learned Special Judge. So, there is no illegally in the matter of taking cognizance as well. According to section 173(3B) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, there is no legal bar to cause further investigation of an offence in respect of which charge sheet has already been submitted in the Court. It transpires that during a long period the misappropriation of bank money has been committed and still new facts of such misappropriation are coming out during investigation as informed by the learned Advocates. 

 11. In such situation, further investigation was needed and it was lawfully ordered by the Court. It is not a correct position to say that the learned Special Judge himself acted as sanction giving authority under Rule 19(ঞ) of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. Because evidently the offences alleged are schedule offences of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and those offences fall under the Rule 15 of the Emergency Power Rules and automatically such Anti-Corruption Commission case shall have to be tried under the Emergency Power Rules. The question of according further sanction under Rule 19(Yeon), 5(kha) of the Rules is misconceived and the said Rule is only applicable to other general offences under the Penal Code as mentioned in the Rule 14 of the Emergency Power Rules 2007, Moreover, the sanction and it's procedural irregularity, even if any, being purely an executive or administrative fiat, should not have been challenged under section 561A of the Code. Because, it was not a part of judicial proceeding. 

 12. It may be mentioned here that the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, being ex-officio Senior Special Judge, can exercise power of transferring the Special Case to other Special Judges Court under Criminal Law Amendment Act, 1958. So, the objection raised in the application with reference Rule 19(0) of the Emergency Power Rules 2007 is not at all tenable. 

 13. There is another aspect in the matter. Petitioners of both the cases have challenged the juridical proceedings including the order of taking cognizance by the Special Judge, which is a judicial order. So, the embargo imposed by Rule 19(Uma) of the Emergency Power Rules will hold the field insofar as it is concerned. According to the said Rule, during the currency of the Proclamation of Emergency, no order of the Court passed in such category of cases can be challenged during investigation and trial. So, the present applications for quashment under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure are not entertainable. 

 14. We have carefully considered the grounds taken in the applications and we find no reason at all to entertain the quashment proceedings of the Special Case No.14 of 2007. As such, the Rules issued and stay orders passed in connection with these two cases are not legally sustainable and those are liable to be discharged.
